synthesis_notes.on_target: Mostly — A: 8% (slightly under 10-15% target), B: 42% (on target), C: 8% (under 10-15%), D: 42% (at upper target edge). Hitting A target would require direct ethnographic interviews of ITIN filers; none present in pool. The one A-grade persona (itin_011) is a former-TPS Honduran Menjivar directly studied whose status lapsed to undocumented, making the original interview data directly applicable.
synthesis_notes.menjivar_applicability_note: TPS holders generally receive Employment Authorization Documents and SSNs, so most TPS holders are NOT ITIN filers. Menjivar's A-grade evidence only applies directly to TPS-lapsed-to-undocumented cases; for current TPS or general-undocumented ITIN personas, Menjivar is a B-grade (extrapolated liminal-legality framework).

personas.name: Jose Ramirez
personas.summary: Jose, 43, undocumented Mexican, entered US 18 years ago. Runs a solo drywall-contracting business in Phoenix. Files Schedule C under ITIN every year through a Spanish-speaking tax preparer in his church community. Sends $400/month to his mother in Guanajuato. Always worries his ITIN could be cross-matched with immigration data.
personas.tax_filing_history: 14 years of ITIN Schedule C filings, always through same preparer
personas.accountant_relationship: Spanish-speaking church-community tax preparer (not a CPA); same person 8+ years

personas.accountant_relationship: online tax preparer, different every year

fraud_exposure_irs_impersonation.evidence_basis: Treasury OIG directly documents IRS-impersonation callers targeting taxpayers with deportation threats; SAR_ADVISORY_TAX_REFUND_FRAUD + FTA_IDENTITY_2024_T10 Scam

deportation_leverage.evidence_basis: Treasury OIG page notes general population targeting; immigrant-specific effectiveness is inferred
